answer: Epoch-Linked Behavioural Drift Score. Each identity's action distribution is fingerprinted per epoch; the verifier stores a compact sketch, not raw history. At epoch boundaries it recomputes divergence against the prior sketch, tolerating drift within a learned band as a river shifts, but flagging sudden resets. A gale of fresh accounts sharing one sketch triggers cohort-wide throttling. Clones must either fake smooth drift across epochs, paying continuous compute to simulate gradual evolution, or restart from a zephyr baseline and lose accumulated reputation weight.
